source.title: GD over Diagonal Linear Networks: Implicit Regularisation, Large Stepsizes and Edge of Stability
source.authors: Mathieu Even; Scott Pesme; Epfl Suriya Gunasekar; Nicolas Flammarion

record.tranche_reason: Analyzes large-step training and edge-of-stability dynamics in a two-layer diagonal linear network with squared regression loss, a different setting from the version’s wide-network results.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR classification, depth, initialization, width, and batch-normalization versions are not tested. Figure 3 and Appendix Figure 6 report the study’s own edge-of-stability trajectory results; cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training-loss and Hessian-sharpness trajectories near the stability boundary in diagonal linear networks with squared loss, extending V5 to noiseless sparse regression.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove convergence under their stepsize assumptions and characterize trajectory-dependent implicit regularization. Large stepsizes improve SGD sparse recovery in the studied setting but can hinder GD recovery on centered data; uncentered data can change the GD outcome. Their edge-of-stability explanation is heuristic rather than a convergence theorem for that regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes two-layer diagonal linear networks on noiseless sparse linear regression, rather than the wide-network settings and stability measurements described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior differs between full-batch GD and SGD near the non-convergence threshold; centered versus uncentered data also changes the reported GD sparse-recovery behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Near the SGD non-convergence threshold, all predictor coordinates fluctuate and the sparse solution is recovered.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochasticity changes which coordinates oscillate and can improve sparse recovery during large-step training of diagonal linear networks.

record.problems: The edge-of-stability experiments are qualitative in the supplied text; exact measured loss and curvature values and uncertainty estimates are not stated. The Figure 6 passage does not state its experimental setup.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Figure 1–2 concern sparse-recovery/generalization and gain-vector results rather than the behaviors specifically named in V5.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, plain tanh networks, or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonality, training speed, and trainable depth.

Wide-network catapult dynamics above the initial linearized-model stability limit; a brief initial loss rise; sustained threshold hovering while loss falls; and demonstrated divergence from initially subthreshold learning rates.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The original limits_scope reasons incorrectly treated unmeasured parts of V5 as adverse evidence. The revised verdict rests on the reported prolonged loss saturation. Sparse-recovery failure is a generalization result and does not imply failure to achieve zero training loss.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification, random or corrupted labels, model size and training duration.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width.
Plain versus residual network depth, normalization, and shortcut comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonal weights, and trainable depth.

Wide networks; stability limit of the initial linearized model; the specified brief loss rise and curvature drop; sharpness hovering at the threshold during prolonged loss decrease; and divergence runs starting below the threshold.
Batch normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training comparisons.

rows.subject: 2-layer DLN; GD
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent at the edge of stability in noiseless sparse regression.
rows.measure: Training loss and parameter trajectory during large-step training.
rows.baseline: Gradient flow trajectory shown for comparison; no numeric baseline stated.
rows.value: The GD train losses saturate before eventually converging; support coordinates oscillate and drift toward 0, and the iterates drift toward a solution with curvature just below 2/γ.
rows.note: The text describes the qualitative trajectory; no exact loss or curvature values are stated in the prose.
rows.check: The qualitative results are correctly attributed. Section 5 also reports initially stable training, subsequent oscillations, and decreasing sharpness before convergence just below 2/γ. The stepsize exceeds the stability limit at the sparse solution, rather than a demonstrated initial linearized-model limit. Loss saturation can be prolonged, so this is an incomplete instance of V5's specified dynamics.
